title: Zero to Recruiter: a Talent Acquisition roadmap
subtitle: An 8-stage path for an absolute beginner in Lagos, Nigeria. About 5 hours a week. Free resources first; paid options are marked and listed separately in the library document.

stages.title: Orientation - what a recruiter actually does
stages.description: Learn the hiring lifecycle end to end, the vocabulary of talent acquisition, and where the recruiter fits alongside hiring managers. No prior HR knowledge assumed.
outcomes: Describe the stages from workforce planning to onboarding
Name the common recruiter roles and the difference between agency and in-house recruiting
Explain why hiring decisions should be based on defined criteria rather than gut feel

resources.title: The HR Learning Lab: HR Essentials (video playlist)
resources.duration: 1 hour for starter lessons and notes (study budget)
resources.why: Start with what HR does, the employee life cycle and the wider HR profession before specialising in talent acquisition.
resources.action: Watch lessons 1-4, then sketch the employee life cycle and explain where recruitment fits. Use remaining study time for notes and review.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-27: public HR Essentials playlist, 16 listed videos; description and initial lesson titles readable without sign-in. The fetch also exposed a YouTube error banner, so playback and mobile app handoff remain untested. Content developed by Dr. Heather Staples; videos produced using AI-supported tools. This is introductory study, not a professional qualification.

resources.title: The HR Learning Lab: Talent Acquisition (video playlist)
resources.duration: About 2 hours of selected lessons and notes (study budget)
resources.why: Short, beginner-oriented lessons on job analysis, workforce planning, recruiting, selection and hiring practice. The fastest way to hear the vocabulary before reading heavier material.
resources.action: Watch the first five lessons and write a one-page diagram of the hiring lifecycle in your own words.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-27: public Talent Acquisition playlist, 43 listed videos, description and lesson titles readable without sign-in; playback and mobile app handoff not tested. Creator discloses AI-supported production; confirm consequential claims against primary sources.

stages.focus: Map the hiring lifecycle and name the recruiter's job.
stages.practice: Draw the hiring lifecycle from workforce planning to onboarding and label who owns each step.
stages.effort_note: This includes a one-hour HR Essentials starter budget; use selected lessons, not both full playlists.

stages.title: Foundations - fair process, job roles and the law
stages.description: Build the ground rules: equal opportunity, job and person requirements, the recruitment and selection sequence, and the legal duties that apply when handling candidate information in Nigeria.
outcomes: Run a full and fair recruitment and selection process step by step
Separate job requirements from person specifications
Recognise the basic compliance duties that apply to candidate data in Nigeria

resources.title: Human resources: recruitment and selection
resources.cost: Free, with a free statement of participation
resources.duration: About 12 hours for the full course; assigned sections 4.2–4.5 only
resources.why: A focused written treatment of job analysis, organisational analysis, job descriptions and person specifications. Sections 4.2–4.5 are a subset of the 12-hour course and add a practical checklist and examples; later advertising, shortlisting and references are not assigned here.
resources.action: Complete sections 4.2–4.5, then draft a one-page job analysis, job description and essential/desirable person specification for one real Lagos vacancy. Keep each requirement tied to the work.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the official OpenLearn course page: the course text is free and its sections can be opened without signing in. A free account is needed to track progress, access all quizzes and activities, and claim the free Statement of Participation. Course content was last updated in 2018 and uses UK equality-law framing; pair it with the Nigerian sources in Stage 7.

resources.title: BUS301: Human Resource Management
resources.cost: Free, with a free completion certificate
resources.duration: About 5 hours for assigned Units 2–3; about 24 hours for the full course
resources.why: A free mixed-media path through staffing plans, job analysis and KSAs, job descriptions/specifications, attraction, screening, interviews, tests and offers. The selected units include readings, videos and practice assessments; U.S. legal material is not Nigerian law.
resources.action: Complete Units 2 and 3 only (about five hours), including their linked readings, videos and practice assessments. Skip performance, compensation and the other units for this stage.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the official BUS301 page and Saylor FAQ: no tuition or fees; a free account is required to enroll; course materials and the course-completion certificate are free, subject to completing the course requirements. U.S. employment-law material is not Nigerian law.

stages.focus: Run a full and fair recruitment and selection process.
stages.practice: Write a one-page fair-process checklist for a small Lagos employer hiring its first employee.
stages.effort_note: The 14-hour figure is a planning allowance for the selected OpenLearn sections, Saylor Units 2–3 and practice.

stages.title: Define the role - job analysis, descriptions and success criteria
stages.description: Before sourcing anyone, learn to work out what the job actually requires and what good evidence of it looks like. Most bad hiring starts here.
outcomes: Turn a vague request into a written job description and person specification
Define measurable hiring attributes before speaking to candidates
Build a simple scorecard that every interviewer can use

resources.title: O*NET OnLine: occupation tasks, skills and knowledge
resources.duration: About 2 hours to analyse one occupation
resources.why: Use O*NET task and skill descriptions to learn how to derive role requirements from the work rather than copying another advert. Treat its U.S. occupation data as a method example, then validate duties against Lagos vacancies.
resources.action: Search O*NET for the practice role, read its tasks and skills, and mark five duties to validate against Nigerian job adverts.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the official O*NET homepage: public occupation search and profile information opened without a sign-in or payment prompt. Account: not required for the public database. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. The classifications and labour-market data are U.S.-based, not Nigerian requirements.

resources.title: Recruiter job description (free public sample)
resources.cost: Free public sample; Workable software trial is separate
resources.duration: About 1 hour to inspect and adapt
resources.why: A worked Recruiter job-description example shows how a role summary, responsibilities and requirements can be organised. Use it as a structural example, not as a copy-ready list of requirements.
resources.action: Compare the sample with the Stage 3 task list for a real Lagos vacancy. Remove unsupported requirements and mark each retained criterion essential or desirable.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on Workable’s Recruiter job-description page: the sample text is publicly readable without payment or sign-in. Account: not required to read. Form: none shown for the sample. Trial: Workable advertises a separate 15-day software trial for posting jobs; it is not needed to study or adapt the sample. Certificate: none offered. The template is generic and should be localised.

resources.title: Structured hiring: Introduction (free worksheets)
resources.cost: Free article and direct worksheet/eBook downloads; no software purchase required
resources.duration: About 2 hours including the worksheets
resources.why: Sets out the six-step structured hiring process: role kick-off, scorecard definition, interview planning, interview kit, sourcing and interviewing, and candidate round-up. It makes you define success before you search.
resources.action: Download the linked worksheet and build a scorecard for your practice role with no more than six attributes.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on Greenhouse Support: the six-step structured-hiring article is readable and links two direct PDF downloads. Account: not required. Form: none shown for the article or downloads. Trial: none needed; Greenhouse software is a separate product. Certificate: none offered. The method is product documentation but transfers to other hiring systems.

stages.focus: Write a job description and a scoring scorecard before sourcing.
stages.practice: Produce a job description, a person specification and a six-attribute scorecard for one real vacancy.

stages.title: Find people - sourcing, Boolean search and candidate experience
stages.description: Learn where candidates are, how to search for them, how to write outreach that gets replies, and how to treat people well while doing it.
outcomes: Build Boolean search strings for a real role
Compare job boards, referrals, pipelines and direct search
Write a short outreach message and a simple candidate experience plan

resources.title: Boolean search cheatsheet: Google operators for sourcing
resources.cost: Free to read; separate Workable software trial not needed
resources.duration: About 1–2 hours to adapt and practise
resources.why: A specific Workable example demonstrates operators such as intitle:, inurl:, site:, OR and exclusions. It teaches the search-string method; its U.S.-oriented examples need local adaptation.
resources.action: Build three Boolean strings for the practice vacancy in Lagos. Test the logic with dummy terms or public search results; do not collect real candidate CVs or personal data for practice.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the individual Workable cheat sheet and its public index: the article and PDF link are readable without payment, sign-in or a content form. Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: a separate 15-day Workable hiring-software trial is advertised in the page footer; it is not needed to use the cheat sheet. Certificate: none offered.

resources.title: Talent Sourcing Strategies (video 16)
resources.duration: 7 minutes
resources.why: A quick tour of employer branding, referrals, job boards, pipelines, CV mining and job fairs, plus the growth-mindset argument for looking past job titles.
resources.action: After watching, pick two sourcing channels that fit a small Lagos employer and explain why you skipped the others.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the public YouTube video page: 6:34, with description and transcript accessible without payment or sign-in. Account: not required for this public listing. Form: none. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. The creator discloses AI-supported production; playback was not tested, and this is an overview rather than a primary authority.

resources.title: How to create a positive experience for candidates
resources.duration: About 1 hour including the outreach exercise
resources.why: Google’s guide covers first contact, interview preparation, communication during delays, offers and declines. It gives a concrete basis for planning a respectful candidate journey.
resources.action: Draft a short first-contact message and a candidate-update plan for the practice role, including interview preparation and a clear delay update. Localise the examples for Lagos.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work guide (updated March 2026). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. The examples describe Google’s own practice, not Nigerian law or a guarantee of outcomes.

stages.focus: Build Boolean strings and a candidate experience plan.
stages.level: Beginner; a defined practice role from Stage 3 assumed.
stages.practice: Compare job boards, referrals, pipelines and direct search for the practice role; build three Boolean strings and a short outreach message, then add a simple candidate-update plan.

stages.title: Screen and shortlist - reading CVs against criteria
stages.description: Turn a pile of applications into a defensible shortlist. Practice consistent screening before you ever speak to a candidate.
outcomes: Screen a CV against the scorecard instead of against your impressions
Write a short phone-screen script with the same questions for everyone
Record evidence for rejections in a way you can defend

resources.title: OpenLearn section 4.10: Shortlisting
resources.modality: Free written course section and activity
resources.cost: Free to read; account only for enrolment, progress and the optional free statement
resources.duration: About 1 hour including the activity
resources.why: A focused revisit to systematic shortlisting against a job specification, with a worked candidate comparison and a short activity. Stage 2 assigned sections 4.2–4.5, not this section.
resources.action: Read section 4.10 and complete its shortlisting activity using the Stage 3 person specification. Record one job-related reason for each decision and check for unsupported assumptions.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the direct OpenLearn section page: the section and activity instructions are readable without signing in. Account: a free account is needed to enrol, save progress, use course activities/quizzes and claim the free Statement of Participation; it is not needed to read this section. Form: account creation only. Trial/payment: none. Certificate: optional free Statement of Participation, not a professional qualification. The course uses older UK examples; use Stage 7 for Nigerian legal material.

resources.title: Screening Candidates (video 24)
resources.duration: 8 minutes 14 seconds
resources.why: A concise overview moves from application forms and CVs through job-related assessments, screening interviews and references. It complements the detailed shortlisting activity rather than replacing its evidence-recording practice.
resources.action: Watch the lesson, map each screening step to a Stage 3 criterion, and draft five consistent job-related phone-screen questions. Use fictional practice records; do not make decisions from protected or irrelevant traits.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the public YouTube page: the 8:14 listing and transcript were accessible without payment or sign-in. Account: not required for this public listing. Form: none. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. Playback was not tested. The creator discloses AI-supported production; the transcript mentions U.S. federal/state rules, which are not Nigerian legal guidance.

stages.focus: Shortlist against criteria and record defensible evidence.
stages.level: Beginner to intermediate; a scorecard from Stage 3 assumed.
stages.practice: Screen ten fictional practice CVs against your Stage 3 scorecard, record one evidence line per decision, then draft five consistent job-related phone-screen questions.

stages.title: Interview and decide - structured interviewing in practice
stages.description: Learn the highest-value skill in this roadmap: asking the same well-designed questions and scoring answers against a written rubric.
outcomes: Write behavioural and hypothetical questions tied to defined attributes
Build a rubric that distinguishes poor, borderline, solid and outstanding answers
Run a mock interview and score it independently of a partner

resources.title: A guide to structured interviewing for better hiring practices
resources.duration: About 2 hours
resources.why: The most important single document in this library. Updated in March 2026, it explains the four parts of structured interviewing, how to define hiring attributes, how to draft questions and follow-ups, and how to score with a shared rubric.
resources.action: Write eight questions for your practice role: four behavioural and four hypothetical, each mapped to a scorecard attribute. Add poor and outstanding scoring anchors, then assemble the questions and rubric using your existing Stage 3 scorecard rather than another template card.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work guide (updated March 2026). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. The guide’s examples and internal results are Google-specific; use the method, not its metrics as local guarantees.

resources.title: Effective interviewer training for better candidate experiences
resources.duration: About 1 hour
resources.why: Shows how to write useful interview feedback, avoid vague comments and personality judgements, and leave time for candidate questions. This is what makes a rubric work in a real panel.
resources.action: After your mock interview, rewrite your feedback using the guide's rules and check whether a stranger could reconstruct the evidence.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work guide (updated March 2026). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. It is guidance, not a formal interviewer qualification.

stages.focus: Ask structured questions and score against a written rubric.
stages.level: Intermediate; a scorecard and interview questions assumed.
stages.practice: Run a 30-minute mock interview with a friend, score it independently, then compare your scores.

stages.title: Offer, onboarding and the law in Nigeria
stages.description: Close the loop: references, offers, onboarding, and the two legal areas that a Lagos-based recruiter will meet immediately - data protection and employment law.
outcomes: Explain the lawful bases for processing candidate data under Nigerian law
Draft a short candidate privacy notice
Read the recruiting provisions of the Labour Act and know when to escalate to a lawyer

resources.title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023: General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025
resources.duration: About 3 hours for the relevant articles
resources.why: A recruiter handles CVs, references and background checks, which are personal data. The GAID sets out the principles, lawful bases, consent rules, information duties for data subjects, breach notification and data processing agreements.
resources.action: Read Articles 15, 16, 17, 18, 27, 33 and 34, then draft a six-line privacy notice you could put on a job application form.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by opening the official NDPC PDF: the document is publicly readable without an account, form, trial or payment; no certificate is offered. I checked its arrangement of articles and opening provisions, not every assigned article or the whole directive. It is regulatory guidance, not legal advice; confirm current law with a Nigerian lawyer.

resources.title: Labour Act, Chapter L1 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004
resources.provider: PLAC Laws of Nigeria (statute copy); ILO NATLEX listing
resources.duration: About 2 hours for Parts I and II
resources.why: Part II is specifically about recruiting, including prohibitions on recruiting without a permit or licence, employer permits, recruiter licences and restrictions. Section 7 covers written particulars of employment terms, which matters when you prepare an offer.
resources.action: Read sections 7, 23, 24, 25, 26 and 71. Write down three questions you would ask an employer before running a search on their behalf.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by opening the public PLAC PDF: no account, form, trial or payment is required; no certificate is offered. This is an official-style reproduction, not a government gazette. The Labour Act dates from 1971/Cap. L1 LFN 2004 and may have been amended or partly superseded; verify current law and seek Nigerian legal advice before acting.

resources.title: A data-driven approach to optimizing employee onboarding
resources.duration: About 1 hour including a checklist exercise
resources.why: The guide describes onboarding check-ins at 30, 90 and 365 days and shows how new-hire feedback can identify support gaps across tools, skills and connection.
resources.action: Use the guide’s survey themes to draft a 30-day onboarding checklist for the practice role, with an owner and one check-in point for each item.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 by reading the full Google re:Work page (August 2025). Account: not required. Form: none shown. Trial: none. Payment: none. Certificate: none offered. The examples describe Google’s own programme; adapt the approach to a Lagos employer.

stages.focus: Handle candidate data and offers under Nigerian rules.
stages.level: Intermediate; the full hiring process from Stages 1 to 6 assumed.
stages.practice: Draft a candidate privacy notice and a 30-day onboarding checklist.

stages.title: Work the process - tools, metrics and getting hired
stages.description: Pull the pieces into a portfolio, learn the numbers recruiters are judged on, and start applying for junior recruiter and HR assistant roles in Lagos.
outcomes: Track a practice pipeline in a free tool and report simple funnel numbers
Present one finished hiring project as a portfolio piece
Apply for entry-level roles with evidence rather than certificates alone

resources.title: Managing Your Contacts With the HubSpot CRM
resources.duration: 20 minutes
resources.why: A free CRM is a practical stand-in for an applicant tracking system while you practise. The Academy's course catalogue is explicitly free and online.
resources.action: Create a free Academy account and use the free CRM tier to add ten fictional practice candidates, label their stages, and produce a simple funnel count. Do not upload real candidate data.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the lesson page and HubSpot CRM product page. Study: the lesson is explicitly free (four videos, 20 minutes). Account: a free Academy account is required; the signup form collects account details and the page states that product updates/promotional emails may be sent. Form: account creation only, no separate lesson form. Trial/payment: the CRM free tier is described as non-expiring and requires no credit card; paid tiers exist but are not needed. Certificate: none is advertised for this lesson.

resources.title: HR Metrics That Support Hiring Decisions (video 43)
resources.duration: 4 minutes 19 seconds
resources.why: A short explanation of hiring measures, including cost per hire, time to fill and selection ratio, with calculation examples. It teaches the concepts; the separate Greenhouse report provides a U.S.-only benchmark case study.
resources.action: Watch the video, note its selection-ratio and time-to-fill formulas, then calculate stage-to-stage conversion rates from your fictional HubSpot pipeline.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on the public YouTube page: the 4:19 listing and transcript were accessible without payment or sign-in. Account: not required for this public listing. Form: none. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. Playback was not tested. The creator discloses AI-supported production; use the definitions as a primer and verify consequential decisions against primary sources.

resources.title: The Hire Standard: Fall 2026 U.S. recruiting benchmarks
resources.cost: Free direct PDF; U.S. hiring data only
resources.duration: About 45 minutes for the executive summary and selected tables
resources.why: A current worked example of application, assessment, interview and hire conversion measures, with comparisons by company size. Treat the figures as a U.S. case study, not Lagos targets.
resources.action: Read the executive summary and selected funnel tables. Note how company size changes the reported rates, then calculate your own practice-pipeline conversions rather than adopting the U.S. averages.
resources.access_note: Checked 2026-10-26 on Greenhouse’s report page and direct PDF. Study: the provider advertises free access and the direct PDF opened without account, payment or a submitted form; the landing page has a free-access/download CTA. Account: not required for the direct file. Form: no form submission was needed at the PDF URL. Trial: none. Certificate: none offered. Data covers U.S. organizations using Greenhouse through August 2026 and is not a Nigerian benchmark.

stages.focus: Track a pipeline, report funnel numbers, build a portfolio.
stages.level: Beginner to intermediate; a completed practice project assumed.
stages.practice: Assemble a portfolio folder: job analysis, advert, scorecard, Boolean strings, screening notes, interview kit and funnel numbers. Then apply to five junior recruiter or HR assistant roles.
